chapterInsights.title: Exponential & Logarithmic Functions
outcomes: Sketch exponential growth and decay curves

chapterInsights.title: Sequences & Series
outcomes: Find the nth term of each sequence

definitions.definition: A sequence with a constant difference (d) between consecutive terms: e.g. 3, 7, 11, 15 (d=4).
A sequence with a constant ratio (r) between consecutive terms: e.g. 2, 6, 18, 54 (r=3).

revisionPrompts: Find the 10th term of the arithmetic sequence 5, 8, 11, ...
Find the sum of the geometric series 1 + 2 + 4 + ... to 8 terms.

chapterInsights.title: Introduction to Calculus (Limits)
outcomes: Define a limit informally and formally
formulas: Factoring to remove holes: cancel common factors

definitions.definition: The value that f(x) approaches as x gets closer to a specific value — written lim[x→a] f(x).
f(x) is continuous at x=a if: f(a) is defined, lim[x→a] f(x) exists, and lim[x→a] f(x) = f(a).

chapterInsights.saContext: Limits are the mathematical foundation for calculus — essential for understanding marginal analysis (marginal cost/revenue) used throughout economics.

A line that touches a curve at exactly one point with slope equal to the derivative at that point.

flashcards.front: State the product rule for exponents.
flashcards.back: aᵐ · aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ — when multiplying powers with the same base, add the exponents.

flashcards.front: Simplify: (3x²y)³
flashcards.back: = 3³ · x⁶ · y³ = 27x⁶y³. Apply the power rule: raise each factor to the power 3.

flashcards.front: Factorise: x² − 9
flashcards.back: = (x − 3)(x + 3). Difference of two squares: a² − b² = (a−b)(a+b).

flashcards.front: What does a⁰ equal (a ≠ 0)?
flashcards.back: a⁰ = 1. Any non-zero base raised to the power zero equals 1.

quizItems.prompt: Simplify: x⁵ · x⁻² =
quizItems.explanation: x⁵ · x⁻² = x^(5+(−2)) = x³. Product rule: add exponents when multiplying same base.

quizItems.prompt: Factorise: 2x² + 5x − 3
What is (a³)² equal to?
quizItems.explanation: Power of a power: (a³)² = a^(3×2) = a⁶.

workedExamples.title: Simplifying Algebraic Fractions
workedExamples.summary: Simplify a fraction by factorising numerator and denominator.

flashcards.front: What is the domain of f(x) = √(x − 4)?
If f(x) = 3x² − 2x + 1, find f(−1).
How does adding k to f(x) transform the graph?
flashcards.back: f(x) + k shifts the graph vertically UP by k units (if k > 0) or DOWN (if k < 0).

flashcards.front: What does the vertical line test check?
flashcards.back: Whether a graph represents a function — if any vertical line intersects the graph at more than one point, it is NOT a function.

quizItems.prompt: The domain of f(x) = 1/(x − 3) is:
quizItems.explanation: The denominator cannot be zero: x − 3 ≠ 0 → x ≠ 3. Domain: ℝ \ {3}.

quizItems.prompt: f(x) = 2x + 5. Find f(−2).
The graph of f(x−2) compared to f(x) is shifted:
quizItems.explanation: f(x − h) shifts the graph h units to the RIGHT. f(x−2) shifts f(x) right by 2.

workedExamples.title: Finding Domain and Range
workedExamples.summary: Determine domain and range for common functions.
workedExamples.problem: Find the domain and range of: (a) f(x) = √(2x − 6) (b) g(x) = x² + 1.

steps.label: (b) Domain of g(x)
steps.explanation: x² is defined for all x. Domain: ℝ (all real numbers).

workedExamples.answer: f(x): Domain [3,∞), Range [0,∞). g(x): Domain ℝ, Range [1,∞).

flashcards.front: What is the slope-intercept form of a line?
flashcards.back: y = mx + c, where m is the slope and c is the y-intercept (value of y when x = 0).

flashcards.front: State the quadratic formula.
flashcards.back: x = (−b ± √(b²−4ac)) / 2a for ax² + bx + c = 0.

flashcards.front: Find the x-coordinate of the vertex of y = 2x² − 8x + 3.
What does the discriminant Δ = b²−4ac tell you?
flashcards.back: Δ > 0: two real roots. Δ = 0: one real (repeated) root. Δ < 0: no real roots (complex roots).

quizItems.prompt: The roots of x² − 7x + 12 = 0 are:
The vertex of y = x² − 6x + 5 is at:
If Δ < 0 for a quadratic equation, there are:
quizItems.explanation: When the discriminant is negative, the square root is imaginary — no real solutions exist.

workedExamples.title: Break-Even Analysis Using Linear Functions
workedExamples.summary: Find the break-even quantity for a SA business.
workedExamples.problem: Thabo's food truck has fixed costs R2 000/day. Variable cost is R15 per meal. He sells each meal for R35. Find the break-even quantity.
workedExamples.answer: Break-even at x = 100 meals per day.

flashcards.front: Solve: 2ˣ = 64
flashcards.back: 2ˣ = 2⁶ → x = 6. Express both sides as powers of the same base.

flashcards.front: State the product law of logarithms.
flashcards.back: log(ab) = log a + log b. The log of a product equals the sum of the logs.

flashcards.front: Convert: log₂(32) = x to exponential form and solve.
What is the shape of an exponential DECAY curve (0 < b < 1)?
flashcards.back: Decreasing from left to right; approaches but never reaches zero (x-axis is a horizontal asymptote). Example: y = (1/2)ˣ.

quizItems.prompt: Solve 3ˣ = 81.

quizItems.explanation: log₁₀(1000) = log₁₀(10³) = 3.

quizItems.prompt: Simplify: log 6 + log 5 − log 3
quizItems.explanation: log 6 + log 5 = log 30. log 30 − log 3 = log(30/3) = log 10 = 1. So answer = log 10.

workedExamples.title: Exponential Growth — Population Model
workedExamples.summary: Apply exponential growth to a SA population model.
workedExamples.problem: A city's population grows according to P(t) = 500 000 × (1.03)ᵗ, where t is years from 2024. (a) What is the population in 2034? (b) When will population double?

flashcards.front: Formula for compound interest.
flashcards.back: A = P(1 + i)ⁿ. A = accumulated amount, P = principal, i = interest rate per period, n = number of periods.

flashcards.front: R10 000 invested at 9% p.a. compounded annually for 4 years. Find A.
Formula for future value of an annuity.
flashcards.back: Fv = PMT × [(1+i)ⁿ − 1] / i. Used when you want to know how much periodic savings will accumulate to.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between nominal and effective interest rates?
flashcards.back: Nominal rate is the stated annual rate; effective rate accounts for compounding within the year. Effective rate > nominal rate when compounding is more frequent than annually.

quizItems.prompt: R5 000 is invested at 10% simple interest for 3 years. Accumulated amount = ?
Compound interest differs from simple interest in that compound interest:
options: Is charged on both principal and accumulated interest
Is lower than simple interest over the same period
Cannot be used for savings accounts
quizItems.answer: Is charged on both principal and accumulated interest
quizItems.explanation: Compound interest earns interest on interest — leading to exponential growth, unlike simple interest which is linear.

quizItems.prompt: The present value annuity formula is used to find:
options: How much you will save over time
The current value of a series of future equal payments
The simple interest on a loan
The doubling time of an investment
quizItems.answer: The current value of a series of future equal payments
quizItems.explanation: PV annuity calculates today's lump sum equivalent of future equal payments — used for home loan calculations.

workedExamples.title: Home Loan Monthly Repayment
workedExamples.summary: Calculate the monthly repayment on a SA home loan.
workedExamples.problem: Sipho takes a R800 000 home loan at 11.5% p.a. compounded monthly for 20 years. Find monthly payment.
workedExamples.answer: Monthly repayment ≈ R8 514. Total repaid over 20 years ≈ R2.04 million.

flashcards.front: Find the 15th term of the arithmetic sequence: 3, 7, 11, 15, ...
Find the sum of the first 10 terms of the arithmetic series 2 + 5 + 8 + ...
Find T₅ for the geometric sequence 3, 6, 12, 24, ...
When does an infinite geometric series have a sum?
flashcards.back: When |r| < 1 (the common ratio is between −1 and 1). S∞ = a/(1−r).

quizItems.prompt: The 8th term of the arithmetic sequence 10, 14, 18, ... is:
The common ratio of the geometric sequence 5, 15, 45, 135 is:
The sum to infinity of 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 + ... is:

workedExamples.title: Compound Interest as a Geometric Sequence
workedExamples.summary: Show how compound interest is a geometric sequence.
workedExamples.problem: R1 000 is invested at 10% compound interest. Show the balance each year as a geometric sequence and find the balance after 5 years.
workedExamples.answer: Balance after 5 years = R1 610.50. The annual balances form a geometric sequence with a=1000, r=1.1.

flashcards.front: Define: lim[x→2] f(x) = L.
flashcards.back: As x gets arbitrarily close to 2 (but ≠ 2), f(x) gets arbitrarily close to L.

flashcards.front: Evaluate lim[x→3] (x²−9)/(x−3).
What are the three conditions for f(x) to be continuous at x = a?
flashcards.back: 1) f(a) is defined. 2) lim[x→a] f(x) exists. 3) lim[x→a] f(x) = f(a).

flashcards.front: What is lim[x→∞] (1/x)?
flashcards.back: 0. As x grows infinitely large, 1/x approaches 0 (x-axis is a horizontal asymptote).

quizItems.explanation: Divide top and bottom by x²: (3 + 2/x) / 1 → 3 + 0 = 3 as x→∞.

quizItems.prompt: f(x) is continuous at x = a if:
options: The limit exists and equals f(a)
quizItems.answer: The limit exists and equals f(a)
quizItems.explanation: Continuity requires: f(a) defined, limit exists, and the limit equals f(a) — all three conditions must hold.

workedExamples.title: Evaluating a Limit by Factorising
workedExamples.summary: Remove the 0/0 indeterminate form and evaluate the limit.

steps.label: Check direct substitution
steps.explanation: x=5: (25−25)/(5−5) = 0/0 → indeterminate form. Cannot substitute directly.

flashcards.front: State the first principles definition of the derivative.
flashcards.back: f'(x) = lim[h→0] [f(x+h) − f(x)] / h.

flashcards.front: Use the power rule to differentiate f(x) = 7x⁵.
The derivative f'(a) gives the slope of the __________ at x = a.
flashcards.back: Tangent line to the curve y = f(x) at the point (a, f(a)).

flashcards.front: Find the equation of the tangent to y = x² at x = 3.

quizItems.prompt: Using the power rule, d/dx[6x⁴] = ?
quizItems.explanation: Power rule: 6 × 4 × x³ = 24x³.

quizItems.prompt: The derivative of a constant c is:
quizItems.explanation: Constants have no rate of change — d/dx[c] = 0.

quizItems.prompt: f'(x) represents the __________ of a function at a point.
quizItems.explanation: The derivative measures the rate at which the function changes at a specific instant — not an average over an interval.

workedExamples.title: Derivative from First Principles
workedExamples.summary: Derive the derivative of f(x) = x² using the limit definition.
workedExamples.problem: Find f'(x) for f(x) = x² using first principles.

steps.label: Expand (x+h)²
steps.explanation: = lim[h→0] [x²+2xh+h² − x²] / h = lim[h→0] [2xh + h²] / h.

steps.label: Factor and cancel h
steps.explanation: = lim[h→0] h(2x + h) / h = lim[h→0] (2x + h) = 2x.

workedExamples.answer: f'(x) = 2x. This confirms the power rule: d/dx[x²] = 2x.

Chapter-by-chapter teaching focus (derived from the module's own learning outcomes and key definitions):

• Chapter 1 — Number Systems & Algebra Review. Emphasise: Apply the laws of exponents; Factorise algebraic expressions; Simplify algebraic fractions. Local context: Algebra underpins all financial calculations — from SARS tax computations to compound interest calculations on home loans.

• Chapter 2 — Functions & Graphs. Emphasise: Define a function and identify domain and range; Use function notation f(x); Sketch and interpret graph transformations. Local context: Functions model real-world relationships: demand as a function of price, cost as a function of output — core tools for SA business analysis.

• Chapter 3 — Linear & Quadratic Functions. Emphasise: Determine the equation of a line given slope and point; Find roots of a quadratic using factorisation or formula; Find the vertex of a parabola. Local context: Break-even analysis in SA business uses linear cost and revenue functions. The break-even point is the intersection — solving a linear equation.

• Chapter 4 — Exponential & Logarithmic Functions. Emphasise: Sketch exponential growth and decay curves; Apply the laws of logarithms; Solve exponential and logarithmic equations. Local context: Exponential growth models compound interest on SA home loans and investment accounts. Logarithmic models appear in Richter scale and sound decibels.

• Chapter 5 — Financial Mathematics. Emphasise: Calculate simple and compound interest; Distinguish nominal from effective interest rates; Calculate future and present value of annuities. Local context: SA home loan calculations use present value annuity formulas. SARS tax tables and retirement annuity planning rely on compound interest and annuity mathematics.

• Chapter 6 — Sequences & Series. Emphasise: Identify arithmetic and geometric sequences; Find the nth term of each sequence; Calculate partial and infinite sums. Local context: Geometric sequences model compound interest growth — the balance after each compounding period forms a geometric sequence with ratio r = (1+i).

• Chapter 7 — Introduction to Calculus (Limits). Emphasise: Define a limit informally and formally; Evaluate limits algebraically; Determine continuity at a point. Local context: Limits are the mathematical foundation for calculus — essential for understanding marginal analysis (marginal cost/revenue) used throughout economics.

• Chapter 8 — Introduction to Derivatives. Emphasise: Find the derivative from first principles; Apply the power rule; Determine the equation of a tangent line. Local context: Derivatives underpin marginal analysis — the foundation of business optimisation (profit max, cost min) applied throughout SA economics and accounting.
